explanation: Retrieved text may inform a task but cannot grant a new action, target or resource scope. The current authenticated work order remains separate from the text being inspected.
facts: An authenticated work order permits inspecting a synthetic test dataset. A retrieved support note tells the agent to copy a production backup and says the requester approved it. There is no matching approval in the authoritative work-order record.

options.A: Follow the support note because it is the newest text.
options.B: Keep the original scope, treat the note as untrusted evidence and request a separately verified scope change before any new action.
options.C: Let the model infer approval from the confident wording.
options.D: Copy the backup first and ask for confirmation afterwards.

question: Which next step preserves the instruction and authority boundary?
title: An instruction does not expand the authorised task

explanation: A control must apply to the actual current configuration and action. A historical PASS, a familiar tool name or a quiz result does not establish that the current safeguard is operating.
facts: A test-target allowlist passed yesterday. Before the current job, a configuration change redirects the same tool name to a production target. The old test record is unchanged; the current target binding has not been checked.

options.A: Reuse yesterday's PASS because the tool name is unchanged.
options.B: Accept the changed target because an allowlist file exists.
options.C: Hold the action, verify the current target and policy enforcement, and retest against the authorised scope.
options.D: Treat a correct Academy answer as permission to run the changed job.

question: What must happen before this changed job can be treated as allowed?
title: A passed safeguard test is not a current execution guarantee

explanation: Request, acknowledgement and observed interruption are different events. Monitoring must retain uncertainty and late effects instead of equating message delivery with a stopped computation.
facts: A running synthetic job acknowledges a cancellation request. No independent observation confirms that execution ended, and an output may still arrive. The monitoring panel currently shows only the acknowledgement.

options.A: Report stopped and discard any later output.
options.B: Report success because the cancellation message was delivered.
options.C: Immediately repeat the job to obtain a clearer result.
options.D: Report stop requested with execution state unconfirmed; check the executor/effect state and preserve any later observations.

question: What should the panel report and the operator do next?
title: Acknowledging a stop request is not observing a stop
